recalled_knowledge.item: Xenophobic isospin ratio f_n/f_p ~ -0.7 (= -Z/N for xenon) and its origin
Multipole selection rule: M_J with even J <= 2 J_nuc, so J <= 1/2 nuclei have a single M_0 multipole (dyad response); 131Xe (J=3/2) also has M_2
recalled_knowledge.presumed_source: Fitzpatrick et al. 2013 / Anand et al. 2014

recalled_knowledge.item: 0-nu-beta-beta-grade enriched xenon is ~90% 136Xe with mostly 134Xe remainder
Two-body (meson-exchange) currents contribute few-30% of the one-body isoscalar M response and are absent from WimPyDD

recalled_knowledge.presumed_source: NREFT spin response structure (Fitzpatrick et al.)

failed_or_abandoned: Locating F_p/F_n zeros as deep local minima of W_pp/W_nn with a neighbour-depth criterion missed second zeros (responses ~1e-6 of W(0), slightly negative from tabulation noise); replaced by sign changes of W_pn = F_p F_n

Dyad test normalised to the q->0 maximum was insensitive (131Xe passed); pointwise ratio over 5-350 keV was noise-dominated near zeros (136Xe failed with deviation 20); final criterion spin-based (J<=1/2) with pointwise check restricted to 5-200 keV, >8 keV from zeros
Minimising N_lo for inelastic delta >= 250 keV is meaningless (5.4-55 keV window kinematically empty); replaced by N_mid = R(55-200)/R(200-270)
rho(248) undefined where the isoscalar reference vanishes at 248 keV (delta = 380 keV Sun-frame, onset 228 keV, node 250 keV); flagged nan
